name: Teresa Lopez
life: “I still remember attending a family dinner in an unfamiliar uniform.” Monday often includes a stop at Paper & Pine Books, where Teresa starts with the handwritten shelf cards and often leaves with a suggestion for somebody else.
voice: I came in uniform because changing clothes would make me late. Half my friends thought I was there to stop the party.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a plum-colored cardigan and one cuff folded back twice. Teresa has a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow, with close-cropped dark curls. Teresa takes off the watch before a long conversation during a conversation.
personality: Teresa has a strong competitive streak and a very soft spot for the person finishing last. A prize tastes better when everybody had enough time to enter.
agenda: To join the reunion without stopping it.
family: Ramona Vargas is Teresa’s half-sibling. Teresa chooses the familiar route. Ramona can stop the walk at any corner. Walking side by side makes it easier to disagree without turning each disagreement into a contest. Asked about *School after sixty*, Ramona says, “I made a clean copy of the practice paper because my partner was embarrassed about crossing out every line.”
connections: Samuel Molina. A uniform and a school nickname briefly belong to the same young-looking person. Also in the story is Basil Allard (schoolmate).

reactions.situation: The person everyone expects to speak wants to sit down
reactions.response: Teresa gives the expected speaker a seat and lets the old classmates start talking amongst themselves.

reactions.situation: A coworker arrives late after a night at the hospital
reactions.response: Teresa writes down the shift time accurately, then helps them explain the circumstances without having to tell the whole room.

reactions.response: Teresa explains exactly what help was offered and offers the same practical help to the accuser.
reactions.asWritten: If accused of favoritism, Teresa explains exactly what help was offered and offers the same practical help to the accuser.
